analysis.title: Americas Utilities: Power - IPPs: Updating estimates into 3Q; pullback presents compelling opportunity for select IPPs with earnings guidance outlook in focus
key_insights: GS forecasts for 3Q26 are 1%/7%/1% above FactSet consensus for VST/NRG/CEG respectively, and TLN estimates are refreshed in this note.
On the 3Q calls GS expects earnings guidance outlooks to be in focus. Strong PJM pricing is expected to blunt weaker ERCOT power price dynamics in the 2027 forward curve.
GS expects updates on NRG's guidance of signing 1 GW of data center demand by year-end, plus broader color on capital allocation and share repurchase plans across the IPPs.

GS sees valuation as attractive after the pullback in IPP shares, which it attributes to macro uncertainty. The IPPs trade at an average 12% FCF yield and ~7.5x EV/EBITDA on GS 2027 estimates, excluding CEG.
CEG trades at a 4.8% FCF yield and 12.1x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates. GS rates TLN, VST and NRG Buy and CEG Neutral.

VST: 3Q EBITDA estimate rises to $2,150mn from $2,054mn on natural gas price moves in Texas. 2027/2028 EBITDA estimates fall to $7,924mn/$8,891mn from $8,103mn/$9,084mn. The price target falls to $200 from $206.

VST: the DOE made a conditional loan commitment of $4.2bn to cover ~433 MW of uprates across the nuclear fleet for PJM assets, preserving ~4 GW of baseload power. It includes an option for the DOE to finance future uprates at Comanche Peak in Texas.

VST: the company will provide 2027 guidance this quarter. GS does not base case a 2028 midpoint, but expects management to outline building blocks toward the longer-term EBITDA and free cash flow outlook.

VST: PJM regulatory developments, including the FERC decision to delay the RBP auction and largely reject the IRAS proposal, are expected to be in focus for the call and for PPA contracting of VST's plants.

NRG: management still targets signing its 1.2 GW hyperscaler project in Texas by year-end. Alternatives if the PPA is not signed are leaning into the buyback or selling the equity interest in the turbine position with a stake in the 2029 COD.
NRG: GS lowers outer-year estimates on weaker Texas pricing in 2027. 3Q EBITDA moves to $1,920mn from $1,945mn and the price target moves to $167 from $169.

NRG: management views buybacks as attractive, with a plan to repurchase at least $1bn annually. GS expects an update on the long-term EPS CAGR of 14%+, FCF before growth outlook and leverage expectations.
NRG: LS Power is more hedged in 2027, limiting exposure to power price upside. GS is encouraged by the 2028 outlook with fewer volumes hedged and expects updated hedge disclosures.

CEG: GS lowers its 3Q estimate to $3.85 from $3.96 on weaker ERCOT pricing. It expects more detail on capex, volumes and ramp schedules for announced PPAs but no full financial plan roll-forward until the 4Q call.
CEG: GS is constructive on fundamentals but sees valuation as less attractive at current levels. Price target rises to $316 from $305.

CEG: GS expects commentary on the FERC delay of the RBP as potentially constructive for bilateral contracting, and on expectations for the December PJM capacity auction clearing price and the FERC-mandated cap, which management would like removed.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $200 from $206 on lower 2027/2028 EBITDA estimates, based on 10.0x EV/EBITDA and a 7.0% FCF yield. GS cites 39% total return potential.
Price target cut to $167 from $169 as the EV/EBITDA multiple falls to 8.50x from 8.75x and FCF yield moves to 9.00% from 8.75%. GS cites 74% total return potential.
Price target raised to $316 from $305 on a 21.0x P/E and 5.0% FCF yield. Valuation is seen as less attractive at a 4.8% FCF yield and 12.1x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates.
Buy rating reiterated, with estimates refreshed in this note.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees the pullback in IPP shares, driven by macro uncertainty, as a compelling opportunity in select names, with Buy ratings on TLN, VST and NRG.

earnings_insights: GS 3Q26 forecasts are 1%/7%/1% above FactSet consensus for VST/NRG/CEG. These are GS estimates ahead of the print, not reported results.

VST: GS 3Q26 EBITDA estimate $2,150mn (up from $2,054mn). GS FY26 EBITDA estimate $7,330mn (up from $7,305mn). GS 3Q26E EPS $2.72, FY26E EPS $8.20 (old $8.11), FY27E $9.40 (old $10.05), FY28E $12.00 (old $12.64).

NRG: GS 3Q26 EBITDA estimate $1,920mn (down from $1,945mn). GS FY26 EBITDA estimate $5,505mn (from $5,530mn). GS 2027-2029 EBITDA estimates $5,851mn/$6,413mn/$6,800mn (old $6,051mn/$6,428mn/$6,857mn). GS FY26E EPS $8.63 (old $8.72), FY27E $10.25 (old $11.01).
CEG: GS 3Q26 EPS estimate $3.85 (from $3.96). GS FY26E EPS $12.00 (from $11.98). FY27E EPS $13.23 maintained. FY28/FY29 EPS estimates $17.10/$19.93 (from $17.09/$19.91).
VST will provide 2027 guidance with 3Q26 results, consistent with prior years. CEG is not expected to roll forward its full financial plan until the 4Q call.
NRG management's long-term EPS CAGR target is 14%+ and the buyback plan is at least $1bn annually.
risk_factors: VST: PJM capacity auction uncertainty, lower than anticipated power prices, and the future of the power demand theme.
NRG: headline risk tied to the AI and data center theme, lower-than-anticipated power prices, and PJM capacity auction price uncertainty.
CEG: regulatory and interconnection risk, lower than anticipated power prices, and a slowdown in data center demand.
NRG: failure to sign the 1.2 GW hyperscaler PPA by year-end could damage the company's credibility.
Weaker ERCOT pricing in the 2027 forward curve.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees the IPPs at a 12% average FCF yield and ~7.5x EV/EBITDA on 2027 estimates (ex-CEG) as attractive after a macro-driven pullback, with strong PJM pricing and data center PPAs supporting earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Weaker ERCOT power prices in the 2027 forward curve, lower 2027 EBITDA estimates for VST and NRG, and the risk that NRG's 1.2 GW data center PPA is not signed by year-end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NRG failing to sign the 1.2 GW hyperscaler PPA by the end of the year, or guidance on the 3Q calls that points to lower 2027 expectations.
